# Kunlun XML fixtures

`kunlun-p800-running-process.xml` and `kunlun-p800-idle-captured.xml` were captured using `xpu-smi -q -x` on 2026-10-19, driver 5.0.21.8, with eight physical P800 cards. The busy node was serving an existing vLLM workload; the idle node had no compute processes. No workloads, driver settings, ECC mode or cards were changed to produce the captures.

Only serials, UUIDs and PIDs were replaced consistently. All card counts, temperatures, power/memory readings, process names, XML structure and the malformed `gpu_instance_id` closing tag are retained. The provenance JSON records hashes before/after redaction; private originals are retained outside Git at `gpuworks/secrets/k26-glm53-fp8-kernels-20261019/node{11,12}-xpu-smi-original.xml`; both raw SHA-256 hashes were reverified on 2026-10-28. The busy original contains 15 `process_info` blocks, and the idle original contains none.

`kunlun-p800.xml` is the historical two-card, anonymized parser fixture. It is not claimed as a contemporaneous idle comparison. Fault mutations in Go tests are synthetic fault injection, not captured vendor output. ECC-disabled and partially enumerated device failures have not been observed in this capture; tests of unknown ECC and absent rows establish conservative behavior only. The process-tag repair is observed on 5.0.21.8, not asserted for all driver versions.

The 2026-10-28 read-only captures are `kunlun-p800-node11-busy-20261028.xml` and `kunlun-p800-node12-idle-20261028.xml`, with matching `-sysfs.json` files containing observed PCI IDs, Kunlun sysfs minor mappings and `/dev/xpu*` device numbers. Their raw JSON files are private under `secrets/kunlun-capture-20261028/`; `kunlun-capture-20261028-provenance.json` records raw and redacted hashes. Both XML commands returned eight rows. Node11 had one `process_info` block, node12 none. `xpu-smi topo -m` timed out after 15 seconds on both and supplied no usable topology output. Serial, UUID and PID values use deterministic one-to-one replacements; UUIDs retain `GPU-` plus UUID syntax and PIDs remain decimal numbers.

A separate read-only follow-up on 2026-10-28 recorded `stat` modes and rdev for `/dev/xpu*`, `/dev/xpuctrl` and `/dev/xdr*`, plus the control sysfs mapping. Each node has ten character devices in this follow-up. The `kunlun-p800-node{11,12}-device-mode-followup.json` files and provenance hashes identify this later observation separately from the XML/sysfs capture; the test checks that the follow-up rdev values match the earlier capture before using the observed character-device modes.

A second, separately timestamped follow-up used `os.lstat` to inspect the device paths themselves without following links. `collect-kunlun-device-lstat.py` is the saved read-only collector. Both nodes reported all ten XPU/control/XDR paths as character devices, and the lstat rdev values matched the earlier stat capture. The 8-card injection test reads the `-device-lstat-followup.json` fixtures, requires `method: os.lstat`, and verifies rdev against the original sysfs fixture. The older `-device-mode-followup.json` remains a distinct `os.stat` observation.
